semantic_findings: Most observed workload is parameterized PostgREST RPC SELECT transport and server-side JSON aggregation, rather than evidence that an index, RPC, or SQL wrapper is unused. Review underlying routines by previously pinned complete-source receipts; do not infer defects from cumulative counts.

The normalized dic_redeem_invite invocation remains present in pg_stat_statements with 18 cumulative calls since October 9 reset, but a fresh public pg_proc and public pg_class check finds no function/relation with that name. It is an historical workload residue, not proof of an active invitation handler. Selected live cloud/client and admin callers did not mention it; no universal source-code absence claim.

The current dic_claim_universal_preview, dic_preview_cached_verified, and dic_preview_preflight routines all remain present; their old accumulated calls alone cannot prove present usage. Do not delete or label RETIRED without comprehensive external consumer and publisher proof. The inspected public preview SQL checks membership and email confirmation, requires unique verified source for cached responses, and retains cooldown across nonadmin preview window rollover.

Cumulative app RPC means in this selected set are at most 61.888ms (coffee match, 41 calls), 51.991ms for client mutation (74 calls), and 15.284ms for personal state (4787 calls). No observed temp blocks in these selected app entries; cumulative since October 9 cannot establish current p95 or latency regression. No justified index/function removal or performance rewrite from these values.
The service_role direct PostgREST subscription SELECT is an intended broker data access pattern, not evidence of public browser access; hosted request/session boundary remains unverified under #96.
